preamble: The close back rounded vowel /u/ lowers to the close-mid back rounded vowel [o], a common vowel shift attested across many language families. This lowering occurs through general vowel-system shifts (as in Turkic historical phonology) and also through emphasis spreading in Arabic dialects, where high back vowels lower in proximity to emphatic consonants.

examples.note: Historical lowering of inherited Proto-Turkic /u/ to /o/ in modern Bashkir. Distinguishes Bashkir from other Turkic languages that maintain /u/. Example: PT *turk → Bashkir torc (strong, mighty).

Similar to Bashkir, Tatar underwent historical /u/ → /o/ lowering. This marks a key phonological distinction between Kazan Tatar and other Turkic varieties. Example: PT *kumush (silver) → Tatar qomosh.
High back vowel lowers to mid-back position due to emphasis spreading from adjacent emphatic consonants (tˤ, dˤ, sˤ, zˤ, qˤ)
Emphasis spreading from emphatic ḍ causes lowering of preceding /u/ in Moroccan varieties
English typically lowers and diphthongizes French /u/ in loanwords. E.g., French 'tour' [tu:ʁ] → English 'tour' [tʊr] or [tor].
PI *u lowers to *o in Northern Iroquoian, after PI *o had become *a
Reconstructed stage. Pre-Samic *u was lowered to *ʊ and then became *o in the vowel shift; Finnish kulke- 'to go'.
